questions.q: What does "selectivity" mean for a SOQL query filter?
options: The fraction of the table's rows the filter is expected to match — lower is more selective and cheaper to serve through an index
Whether the query uses SELECT * or names specific fields
Whether the query is written in a trigger versus a class
The number of relationship levels the query traverses
questions.explain: Selectivity is about how much of the table a filter narrows down to. A highly selective filter matches a small slice of rows, which is exactly what makes an index worth using.

questions.q: On a standard-indexed field, what is the approximate selectivity threshold for the first million records in a table?
options: Under 100% — any filter on a standard index is always considered selective
Under 5% of the first million records (that's the custom-index threshold instead)
There is no threshold for standard indexes, only for custom indexes
Under 30% of the first million records
questions.explain: Salesforce's query optimizer treats a standard-indexed filter as selective if it targets under 30% of the first million rows (dropping to 15% beyond that, capped at 1 million rows total).

questions.q: Why does WHERE CALENDAR_YEAR(CloseDate) = 2026 typically defeat an index on CloseDate, while WHERE CloseDate >= 2026-01-01 AND CloseDate <= 2026-12-31 does not?
options: CALENDAR_YEAR() is not valid SOQL syntax and would simply fail to compile
Wrapping the field in a function means the optimizer can no longer use the index on the bare field directly, while a plain range comparison on the unmodified field can still use the index
Date fields can never be indexed in Salesforce under any circumstance
The two queries return different results, so the comparison isn't meaningful
questions.explain: Wrapping an indexed field in a function generally defeats the index because the optimizer can't match the function's output back to the index's stored values — rewriting the same intent as a bare-field range comparison lets the index apply.

questions.q: What does the Developer Console's Query Plan tool actually show you?
options: The exact number of milliseconds a query took to execute on the last run
A list of every governor limit consumed by the current Execute Anonymous window
The optimizer's real chosen execution plan and estimated cost for a query, including whether it's using an index or falling back to a table scan
A visual diagram of all objects and their relationships in the org
questions.explain: The Query Plan tool exposes the optimizer's actual decision — its cost estimate and whether the chosen path is index-driven or a TableScan — rather than leaving you to guess based on selectivity math alone.

questions.q: Why is naming only the fields a transaction actually needs part of query optimization, separate from selectivity?
options: Because unnecessary fields increase heap usage and, for relationship queries, every additional traversed relationship adds real cost, regardless of how selective the filter itself is
Because SOQL enforces a hard limit of 5 fields per SELECT clause
Because unused fields are automatically stripped by the platform and have no actual cost
Because field selection has no measurable effect on performance in Salesforce
questions.explain: A query can be perfectly selective and still waste resources if it pulls far more fields (or relationship data) than the operation uses — that cost shows up in heap size and data volume, independent of whether an index was used.
